claims.text: A Fabric tenant is a single organizational instance of the service aligned one-to-one with a Microsoft Entra tenant; inside it, workspaces act as collaboration containers that hold items, draw compute from a capacity, and control who can access their contents.

In Fabric vocabulary, an item is any object you create — lakehouse, notebook, warehouse, eventhouse, and so on — and each workload contributes its own item types; a workload is the collection of capabilities aimed at one functional area, such as Data Engineering or Real-Time Intelligence.

A capacity is a dedicated pool of resources that performs work in Fabric, and capacity units (CUs) are the single unit of compute measurement: every workload and operation draws CUs from the available capacity, with consumption classified as either interactive or background operations.

Delta Lake is the standard table format across all Fabric workloads — data ingested into Fabric is stored as Delta tables by default — which is what lets different engines read each other's output without conversion.
V-order is a write-time optimization of the parquet format that speeds up reads, and all Fabric engines write v-ordered parquet files by default.

Domains let an organization group workspaces into logical business areas (for example Finance or Marketing), giving administrators a level above the workspace at which to delegate management and apply governance policies.

A lakehouse is a database built over the data lake that holds files, folders, and tables; it is served by both the Apache Spark engine and the SQL engine, and gains ACID transaction support when its tables use the open Delta format.

A SQL analytics endpoint provides T-SQL querying over items that are not warehouses themselves — it is available for lakehouses, mirrored databases, and SQL databases in Fabric — while the warehouse item supplies full transactional T-SQL like a traditional enterprise data warehouse.
Real-Time Intelligence storage is hierarchical: a workspace can contain multiple eventhouses, an eventhouse can contain multiple KQL databases, and each KQL database can contain multiple tables.

Direct Lake is a semantic-model storage mode in which the model reads Delta tables straight from OneLake, avoiding both data import and DirectQuery, and so pairs import-like performance with DirectQuery-like freshness.

Dataflow Gen2 is the low-code Data Factory interface for ingesting and transforming data from hundreds of sources; it is distinct from Power BI's Dataflow Gen1, and there is no upgrade path from Gen1 to Gen2.

A shortcut is an embedded reference inside OneLake that points at another file-store location, giving workloads access to external operational data without copying it or building ETL pipelines, and it can be combined with cross-tenant data sharing for governed external access.
